# modgrad-obs

> Training observability for LLM pre-, mid- and post-training runs: metrics,
> events and summaries stored as append-only JSONL, a live dashboard, and
> analysis (trends, honest forecasts, spikes, divergence, seed noise) that
> runs in the client, never on the server. This file is the quickstart for
> coding agents. It is complete: you should not need anything else.

Binaries: `obs` (CLI and MCP server) and `obs-server` (HTTP API, dashboard).
Install from a checkout of https://github.com/rotkonetworks/modgrad:

    cargo install --path crates/modgrad-obs          # -> obs
    cargo install --path crates/modgrad-obs-server   # -> obs-server

Note: OBS Studio also installs a binary called `obs`. If `obs --help` does
not print this tool's usage, use the full path (usually `~/.cargo/bin/obs`).

Data lives in an obs directory (default `./obs`): `obs/runs/<run>/` holds
`config.json`, `metrics.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `summary.json`. Run names are
1 to 3 `/`-separated parts of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, e.g. `sweep/lr3e-4_s1`.
Name seeds `<config>_s1`, `<config>_s2`, ...: the tools group them and test
differences against seed noise.

## The four doors

Every door ends in the same place: a run with metrics you can query and chart.

1. MCP: `obs mcp`. An agent reads and writes runs through 7 tools. Use this
   to answer questions about runs ("did it diverge?", "worth continuing?").
2. `obs run -- <command>`: wraps a training command, passes its output through
   unchanged, parses metric lines from stdout/stderr, and samples CPU/RSS/GPU.
   No code change. Use this to instrument a script that already prints metrics.
3. HTTP API: `POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/<run>/log` with JSON. Any language, no
   client library. Use this inside a training loop or framework callback.
4. The dashboard: `obs-server` serves it at `/`. `$OBS/#new` creates an
   anonymous project and shows ready-to-paste commands; `#run=<id>`,
   `#project=<p>` and `#board=<id>` open a run, a project or a saved board.
   Log files (CSV, JSONL, text logs, TensorBoard, W&B offline) can also be
   dropped onto the page.

## 1. MCP

Local data (recommended; nothing else to run):

    obs mcp --dir ./obs                                        # or OBS_DIR=./obs

Against an obs-server (the tools fetch rows and analyse locally; the server
only stores and selects):

    obs mcp --url https://obs.example.org --token obsp_...    # or OBS_MCP_URL=... OBS_TOKEN=...

A server started with `obs-server --mcp` also serves MCP over streamable HTTP
at `$OBS/mcp`. That is for agents that cannot run a local binary: the
analysis then runs on the server. Prefer `obs mcp --url` when you can.

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add obs -- obs mcp --dir ./obs
    claude mcp add --scope project obs -- obs mcp --dir obs          # writes .mcp.json
    claude mcp add obs --env OBS_TOKEN=obsp_... -- obs mcp --url https://obs.example.org
    claude mcp add --transport http obs https://obs.example.org/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer obsp_..."

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and any client that takes the common JSON shape
(`.mcp.json`, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Cline, ...):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "obs": { "command": "obs", "args": ["mcp", "--dir", "obs"] }
      }
    }

Remote store, local analysis:

    { "mcpServers": { "obs": { "command": "obs", "args": ["mcp", "--url", "https://obs.example.org"],
                               "env": { "OBS_TOKEN": "obsp_..." } } } }

Hosted endpoint (only if the agent cannot run `obs`):

    { "mcpServers": { "obs": { "url": "https://obs.example.org/mcp",
                               "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer obsp_..." } } } }

Tools (arguments are flat and forgiving; run and metric names are fuzzy):

    list_runs(filter?)                    runs with last step, metric count, status
    read_metric(run, metric, last?)       recent values, min/max/last, NaN/inf warning
    summarize(run, metric?, target?)      Verdict line (DIVERGED / OVERFITTING / improving /
                                          no clear progress), trend, spikes and what changed
                                          before them, honest forecast ("no skill" when it
                                          cannot beat the last value), ETA to target, seeds
    compare(runs, metric)                 aligned table, best run, diverged runs; seed groups
                                          (x_s1, x_s2, ...) get mean ± sd and WITHIN/BEYOND noise
    log(run, metrics, step?)              record values; creates the run
    ingest_log(run, text)                 parse pasted stdout into a run
    make_board(query)                     save a dashboard board, return its URL;
                                          query = metric{run=~"a|b"}; several panels with ';'

Typical calls:

    summarize(run="sweep/lr3e-4")                         "is it worth continuing?"
    compare(runs="sweep/*", metric="val_loss")            "which run diverged?"
    compare(runs="abl/base_s*,abl/wd_s*", metric="val_loss")   "is the difference real?"
    summarize(run="long/a", metric="val_loss", target=2.0)     "when will it reach 2.0?"
    make_board(query='reward{run=~"rl/ppo_a|rl/ppo_b"}; kl{run=~"rl/ppo_a|rl/ppo_b"}')

Report what the tools say. If summarize says the forecast has "no skill",
do not give a confident number.

## 2. obs run

    obs run --offline --name exp1 -- python train.py      # writes ./obs/runs/exp1
    obs run --name exp1 -- python train.py                # streams to $OBS_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8790)
    obs run --server https://obs.example.org --token obsp_... --project team --name exp1 -- torchrun ...

Lines it understands (one metric line per print is enough):

    step 1250: loss 3.48 acc 7.5%
    iter 100 | loss=2.31 | lr 3e-4
    [epoch 2/10] train_loss: 0.45
    {'loss': 0.41, 'learning_rate': 5e-05, 'epoch': 0.3}     (HF Trainer's default output)
    tqdm postfixes: 100%|####| 500/500 [00:12<00:00, loss=0.31]

A line without a step uses the last step seen. The child's exit code is
returned. If the server is unreachable, rows are spooled to disk and
`obs push <spool dir>` resends them. `obs tail <run>` prints the latest
values with sparklines.

To instrument a silent script: add one print per logging step, e.g.
`print(f"step {step} loss={loss:.6f} lr={lr:.3e}", flush=True)`, then wrap it
with `obs run`.

## 3. HTTP API

Full reference, plain text: `curl $OBS/api/v1`. Bodies are JSON whatever the
Content-Type; errors are JSON with a corrected example.

    obs-server --root obs --dev                     # local server; --dev = writes need no token
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/projects               # -> {"project", "token": "obsp_...", "board"}
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/log -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBS_TOKEN" \
         -d '{"step": 10, "loss": 0.52, "acc": "71.5%"}'
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/log -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBS_TOKEN" \
         -d '{"rows": [{"step": 11, "loss": 0.5}], "events": ["lr drop"], "config": {"lr": 3e-4}}'
    python train.py 2>&1 | curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/text -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBS_TOKEN" --data-binary @-
    curl -X POST $OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/finish -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBS_TOKEN" -d '{"exit_code": 0}'
    curl "$OBS/api/index"                                       # runs (a project token scopes it)
    curl "$OBS/api/v1/runs/exp1/history?keys=loss,acc&stride=10" # {"steps", "t", "columns"}

The first `log` creates the run. `step` is optional (default: last + 1).
Nested objects flatten with `/`. Re-sending a row is harmless. With a
project token, a run id without `/` lands in the token's project.

## Framework snippets

All of these post to the HTTP API with `requests`; each logging call is one
small POST. Set `OBS_URL` (and `OBS_TOKEN` unless the server runs `--dev`).
Never let logging crash training: catch and drop errors.

    import os, requests
    OBS = os.environ.get("OBS_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8790")
    HDR = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OBS_TOKEN']}"} if os.environ.get("OBS_TOKEN") else {}

    def obs_log(run, step, metrics, **envelope):
        """envelope: config={...}, events=[...], summary={...}, finish=True"""
        body = dict(envelope)
        if metrics:   # step=None means "one past the run's last step"
            body["rows"] = [{**metrics, **({"step": step} if step is not None else {})}]
        try:
            requests.post(f"{OBS}/api/v1/runs/{run}/log", json=body, headers=HDR, timeout=5)
        except requests.RequestException:
            pass

PyTorch loop:

    obs_log("exp1", 0, {}, config={"lr": lr, "batch_size": bs})
    for step, batch in enumerate(loader):
        loss = model(batch).loss
        loss.backward(); opt.step(); sched.step(); opt.zero_grad()
        if step % 10 == 0:
            obs_log("exp1", step, {"train/loss": loss.item(), "lr": sched.get_last_lr()[0]})
    obs_log("exp1", step, {"val/loss": evaluate(model)}, finish=True)

Hugging Face Trainer:

    from transformers import TrainerCallback

    class ObsCallback(TrainerCallback):
        def __init__(self, run):
            self.run = run
        def on_train_begin(self, args, state, control, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero:
                obs_log(self.run, 0, {}, config=args.to_sanitized_dict())
        def on_log(self, args, state, control, logs=None, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero and logs:
                obs_log(self.run, state.global_step, logs)   # non-numeric values are skipped
        def on_train_end(self, args, state, control, **kw):
            if state.is_world_process_zero:
                obs_log(self.run, state.global_step, {}, finish=True)

    trainer = Trainer(..., callbacks=[ObsCallback("sft/run1")])

(Or no code at all: `obs run --name sft/run1 -- python train.py` parses the
dicts the Trainer prints.)

PyTorch Lightning:

    from lightning.pytorch.loggers.logger import Logger
    from lightning.pytorch.utilities import rank_zero_only

    class ObsLogger(Logger):
        def __init__(self, run):
            super().__init__()
            self._run = run
        @property
        def name(self): return "obs"
        @property
        def version(self): return self._run
        @rank_zero_only
        def log_hyperparams(self, params, *a, **kw):
            params = params if isinstance(params, dict) else vars(params)
            obs_log(self._run, 0, {}, config={k: (v if isinstance(v, (int, float, str, bool)) else str(v)) for k, v in params.items()})
        @rank_zero_only
        def log_metrics(self, metrics, step=None):
            obs_log(self._run, step, metrics)
        @rank_zero_only
        def finalize(self, status):
            obs_log(self._run, 0, {}, summary={"status": status}, finish=True)

    trainer = L.Trainer(logger=ObsLogger("pretrain/run1"))

Rust (modgrad SDK): `modgrad_obs::Run::create(...)` and `run.log_scalars(step, &[("loss", x)])`
write the same directory format with no server.

## Viewing

    obs-server --root obs --dev          # then open http://127.0.0.1:8790/
    # boards from make_board open at http://127.0.0.1:8790/#board=<id>
